facts.fact: The Rights and Liberties Committee's minutes of 17 February 2026 record sponsors presenting a 132-article organic-law proposal on personal data that regulates the use of AI, gives a right not to be subject to a solely automated decision and requires impact assessment for high-risk processing; the committee decided to continue examining it.

facts.fact: The committee minutes record the sponsors of a 132-article personal-data organic-law proposal saying it includes a chapter on processing personal data using AI, and the committee decided on 17 February 2026 to continue examining it.

facts.fact: The Assembly's Rights and Liberties Committee heard the sponsors of a 132-article organic-law proposal on personal data protection, to replace the 2004 law, on 17 February 2026 and decided to continue examining it.
facts.system: Organic-law proposal on personal data protection (proposal 95/2025)

facts.fact: The minutes say the proposal reshapes the data protection authority, adding a chamber for financial sanctions, while MPs raised that the authority has been practically absent since 2024.

TUN.note: Only MPs' calls to bar hosting health data abroad and a general remark on sovereignty; no policy, rule or hosting stated.
